#227 correctness review, round 1: PASS WITH NOTES

Exact head: f91b3ffffea45b678dd35a8d9460d4a9e50703a0.

No correctness findings in the ten-file delta. Reviewed the consumers of both narrowed registration snapshots, not only SQL equivalence to RelatedSeats::matches.

Predicate coverage:

| Consumer | Why every potentially relevant row remains |
| --- | --- |
| explicit_session_conflict; direct existing-ID lookup | The original claim ID is in ids, even when its recorded session/process/pane differs. |
| registration_target; native_prebind | Native session selection matches harness_session; spawn prebind/fallback requires the claim's same nonempty pane; explicit fallback matches the named ID. |
| native_supersedes; predecessor validation | An explicit predecessor is in ids. An inferred predecessor shares the claim's process and pane, so the PID/pane relation includes it. |
| Multiple-address count; unknown_session; spawn_predecessor | All inspect the same harness_session; that relation includes every harness and every retirement state. |
| Native owner, supersession and pane-conflict checks | Candidates must match a named/selected row, process, session or pane. The relation is a union, not an intersection, and PID matching deliberately includes other start times. |
| paneless_target | Every inspected candidate shares the claim's native session or PID. Retired rows and foreign harness/process-incarnation conflicts remain present. |
| Observed-dead owner and spawn-prebind revalidation | Their IDs are explicitly carried, so a row remains visible even if all of its other identifying fields changed before the lock was acquired. |
| Ordinary collision check | It requires the claim's exact process identity, a subset of the PID relation. |
| Retired continuity, owner-close and preserved metadata | These consult the selected existing descriptor itself. There is no recursive predecessor/parent-chain traversal through the old roster to truncate: session/spawn/process continuity and the inherited parent are fields of that descriptor. Other services' own keyed reads remain unchanged. |

SQL list_related and the trait default preserve ID ordering and include retired rows. Therefore find/min_by_key tie behavior is preserved. The F162 early return remains a refusal-only brake, and both its snapshot and the locked checks include its explicit/inferred holder candidates.

ID uniqueness no longer relies on the narrowed snapshot: native/paneless minting uses first_free_id under the same registration lock, checking Registry::get for each candidate against all live and retired rows. A candidate omitted by the relation cannot be mistaken for free. This retains the existing mutation/exclusion model rather than introducing a cache.

Live-loop equivalence: PaneObserver's wanted set already excluded tombstoned rows. Both binders' pending predicates already required their exact harness and no tombstone. Both native-receiver retain/reconcile predicates already required live Copilot rows. Cleanup of tracked panes and removal of missing/retired receiver entries still occurs; no omitted retired descriptor was needed for those actions.

Proof: clean detached tree; just pr-freeze 227 returned FINAL with remote/GitHub head agreement, CLEAN and all latest checks passed. CI run 42786679272 is successful at this head: 2,429 Rust tests passed, six skipped. Successful-job JUnit artifact 13749985074 records both shared registry contracts passing, including live_only and each relation/union/order control. It also records passing the old-session holder-current regression, explicit supersession mismatch cases, observed-owner drift revalidation, historical/native and retired-paneless tie selection, retired continuity, prebind/spawn correlation and minted-ID grammar cases. The artifact includes 108 registration, 14 pane-observer, three Claude-binder, seven Codex-binder and 61 delivery-named tests with zero failures. These are the observed CI selector counts, not a local rerun. git diff --check is clean.

No reviewer-local builds, dependency changes, product edits, credentials or daemon/lifecycle operations. No new loop, timer or launch. The existing observer remains 600 ms, and the binders/native reconcile remain on the existing delivery cadence. SQLite still scans rows; the change narrows Rust decoding, not database scan complexity.

Note owed, nonblocking per packet: performance owns the live post-deploy CPU/hot-path sample plus matching ping spawn deltas and spawn-rate receipts. This verdict verifies the row-selection semantics, not an independently measured deployed CPU reduction.
